chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about the miscarried child (siqt), how to deal with it. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'The miscarried child is buried with its blood, in its place.'
ai.seo_question: How is a miscarried child buried according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the ritual status of the siqt (miscarried fetus) by instructing that it be buried in its place of delivery along with its blood, distinguishing its treatment from that of a full-term infant. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that the siqt is treated with respect but does not always carry the full legal weight of a born child regarding inheritance or funeral prayers, emphasizing the sanctity of life from conception while acknowledging developmental stages.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ai Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Al Fazl who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about the miscarried child, how to deal with him. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to me: ‘The miscarried child would be buried with its blood, in its place (straight away)’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mehran from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who has said the following:
“I once wrote to abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asking about what is done for a miscarried child. He (the Imam) wrote to me, ‘A miscarried child is buried with his blood in his place (right away).”’
